HomeAll projectsLLM Latency Tracker

OBSERVABILITY / OPEN DATA

Measure the API from where it is used.

Regional probes turn API response measurements into dated, inspectable datasets for people and AI agents.

ProjectLLM Latency Tracker
ScopePublic implementation and datasets
StackPython · SQLite · JSON API · MCP

The problem

A provider's response time varies by region, request type and measurement window. A single latency number hides those differences and can confuse network responsiveness with model generation speed.

My contribution

  • Built regional edge probes and optional inference probes for AI providers.
  • Implemented central aggregation, historical snapshots and regional percentile statistics.
  • Published the results through a website, JSON datasets, Markdown pages and MCP.

How the system works

Regional probesMeasurementsAggregationDated datasetWebsite / API / MCP

Separate network and inference timing. Edge TTFB and inference TTFT are different measurements. Keeping them separate makes the resulting comparisons easier to interpret.

Keep the probe runtime small. The edge-probe core uses Python's standard library; optional inference probes use provider credentials.

Publish the evidence. Daily snapshots and historical data accompany the interface, so results can be reused and checked outside the website.

What you can verify

The repository contains probe and aggregation code, deployment instructions and dated datasets. The public site exposes rankings and a JSON API, with MCP access for agent workflows.

Source repositoryLive rankingsPublished JSON data

Scope & limitations

Measurements describe a particular region, probe type and time window. Edge TTFB is not a benchmark of model generation speed, and provider rankings change as new measurements arrive.
